Both Lamido and some of his aides have even come out to insist that he is still a force to reckon with in the politics of Jigawa. What they are not saying is that the PDP, in which Lamido remains, is no longer what it used to be.
It does not even have a presidential candidate, at least as far as the electorate is concerned.
Yet the former governor has paraded candidates to wrestle seats from APC senators, with his own son contesting for governor.
Are the APC and Governor Umar Namadi really that weak in Jigawa, or is Lamido misreading the times?
